quickAnswerTitle: Quick Answer: Which Mens Shirt Collar Types Are Best?
quickAnswer: The Semi-Spread collar is the most versatile among all mens shirt collar types, balancing medium-width suit lapels with or without a tie. If you have a round face, choose a Classic Point collar to lengthen your features. If attending formal black tie galas, a specialized wing tip collar is required.
intro: The collar is the most important anatomical component of any shirt. Because it sits directly beneath your chin, it frames your facial structure, dictates your necktie knot choice, and determines whether an outfit leans formal or casual. Understanding different mens shirt collar types ensures you never look mismatched in business suiting or casual tailoring.

sections.heading: 1. The Semi-Spread Collar: The Modern Corporate Benchmark
paragraphs: A semi-spread collar features point tips positioned approximately 3.5 to 4 inches apart. It strikes a balance between conservative point collars and dramatic British cutaways.
It effortlessly accommodates medium-sized tie knots—such as the Half-Windsor and Four-in-Hand—while maintaining enough structure to stand upright when worn open-collar under a blazer.

To keep your spread collar crisp and prevent it from curling under jackets, we recommend using these [Heavy Duty Metal Collar Stays on Amazon](https://link.amazon/B03HVtnAW). They keep collar points razor sharp all day.

bullets.label: Best Face Shape
bullets.text: Universally flattering on oval, angular, and rectangular face profiles.

sections.heading: 2. The Classic Point Collar: The Face-Lengthening Traditionalist
paragraphs: Classic point collars feature narrow spreads (less than 3 inches between points). The vertical direction of the points creates an optical illusion that draws the eye downward.
Men with rounder faces or shorter necks benefit significantly from point collars, as the sharp downward angle creates a slimming, vertical elongation.

sections.heading: 3. The Formal Wing Tip Collar for Black Tie Events
paragraphs: The wing tip collar features small standing collar points that resemble bird wings folded downward. It is the most formal collar in existence.

Wing tip collars are strictly reserved for tuxedo suiting and black tie events. Never wear a wing tip collar to a standard business meeting or casual event; it must always be paired with a black silk bow tie and formal tuxedo stud set for authentic black tie elegance.

sections.heading: 4. The Button-Down Collar (OCBD): The Ivy League Icon
paragraphs: Originally borrowed from polo players who needed to keep their collars from flapping in the wind, the Oxford Cloth Button-Down features small button holes that secure the points to the shirt body.
A quality button-down collar features an unlined, soft construction that forms a relaxed S-shaped curve (the famous collar roll). Pair it with tailored chinos for quintessential business casual.

sections.heading: 5. The Cuban / Camp Collar: The Retro Resort Staple
paragraphs: Unlike formal folded neckbands, the camp collar lays completely flat against your clavicle, creating a continuous open V-neck notch lapel. It contains zero interior stiffeners and is strictly designed for casual warm-weather tailoring.

faqs.question: Can you wear a tie with a button-down collar?
faqs.answer: Yes. An Oxford cloth button-down with a knit silk tie or repp-stripe collegiate tie is a foundational staple of classic American business casual.

faqs.question: What collar should you wear for a black tie event?
faqs.answer: A classic wing tip collar or a formal spread collar with French cuffs is required for black tie tuxedo dress codes.

faqs.question: What is the difference between spread and cutaway collars?
faqs.answer: Spread collars feature points angled outward at roughly 45 degrees. Cutaway collars feature extreme horizontal spread (nearly 180 degrees), revealing the entire tie knot and shirt band.
